title: credential-fuse-pausable-stream-lifecycle-tri-sdk-bump
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces pausable/resumable stream lifecycle, cross-SDK credential handoff (credential-fuse), exposes retry-decision telemetry and new retry preset profiles. Minor SDK version bumps: py 1.22.0 -> 1.23.0, ts 2.9.0 -> 2.10.0, go 1.8.3 -> 1.9.0.
description: Summary: This PR implements a cross-language ergonomic surface for pausable/resumable streaming consumers, and a lightweight credential handoff mechanism we call 'credential-fuse' that reduces reauth churn during short-lived auth windows. Motivation: several teams reported latency spikes and redundant reauth calls during bursty streaming workloads; debugging showed frequent credential refresh races and lack of a clean pause/resume lifecycle on client streams. Goals: 1) provide pausable stream primitives that preserve local cursor/offset state, allow explicit credential handoff with minimal RPC, and provide telemetry for retry decisioning; 2) harmonize ergonomic APIs across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs so examples and migration paths are consistent; 3) surface retry hints and a small set of typed retry presets to make opt-in behavior explicit. What changed (high level): - SDK Python: added StreamController.pause()/resume(), StreamContext.attach_credential_fuse(), small refactor of session manager to support short-lived fuse leases, new RetryPreset enum and telemetry labels (retry.reason, retry.hint). - SDK TypeScript: introduced StreamHandle.pause()/resume(), exported types for CredentialFuse and RetryPresets; simplified backoff constructor to accept named presets. - SDK Go: added stream.PausableStreamer interface, CredFuse struct and AttachFuse helper; exported RetryPreset constants and telemetry tags. - Core API compatibility: extended transport handshake to optionally carry a short-lived fuse token and a resume cursor; compatible fallback maintains old handshake shape. - Telemetry/CI: added new retry decision metrics (sdk.retry.decisions), fuse churn counters (sdk.auth.fuse_attempts), and stream lifecycle spans. - Docs/examples: updated tri-sdk examples repository with pause/resume demo and recommended retry presets for conversational and low-latency workloads. - Tests: added unit and integration tests for pause/resume semantics, credential transfer safety, and telemetry emission. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged; fuse usage is opt-in. If server does not support fuse header, SDKs fall back to standard refresh flow. Migration notes: see README updates in SDK folders — primary change for integrators is replacing manual reconnect logic with StreamController.pause/resume when a transient auth flow is desired. Security notes: fuse tokens are single-use bearer tokens with TTL <= 30s and are logged only as hashes in telemetry. Checklist: - [x] API design review with platform (ENG-2419) - [x] Unit tests for Python/TS/Go - [x] Integration e2e against staging runtime - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Docs + examples updated - [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated Performance: soldering fuse reduced reauth RPCs by ~67% in our internal canary (conversational agent workload) and improved median p95 reconnect latency by ~18ms in burst tests. Rollout plan: feature gated by server capability flag. We'll ship SDKs immediately; server-side acceptor will be rolled to staging for 48h canary, then gradual rollout to prod. Related work: builds on earlier retry-presets and session-lease efforts; references: Linear ENG-2419, PM-735.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you clarify the lifetime guarantees of the fuse token? Is it tied to the stream or the session?
Priya Nair: Reply: fuse tokens are single-use and tied to a stream resume event. Session-level refresh still occurs on regular TTL paths; fuse is a short-circuit to avoid full refresh on a handoff.
Lena Müller: Small nit: TS naming 'StreamHandle' vs 'StreamController' in Python — can we harmonize for discoverability?
Priya Nair: Reply: Renamed TS type to StreamController in a follow-up commit b2e7a2d for parity.
Owen Reed: Tests flaked on Go race detector in initial run; suggest adding a small backoff in test harness. Omitted change pushed in c3d9f4b.
Security review (auto): Are fuse tokens ever persisted? Answer: no — only ephemeral in memory and hashed telemetry.

notes_for_release_engineers: Server accepts optional Fuse header X-Redwood-Fuse (base64 token). If you see increased 403s during canary, rollback server fuse-acceptor feature flag and SDKs will gracefully fallback. Watch metrics sdk.auth.fuse_attempts and sdk.auth.fuse_failures.
